text:
Maya (oncall-eng): :rotating_light: paging: customer Lysander (VPC/dedicated pool) reporting token usage mismatch vs billing meter. seeing spike in meter for tenant lys-987 but runtime logs show lower token consumption. starting triage.
incidents-bot: Incident created — ID INC-2026-0421. Severity: P2. Notifying on-call.
Maya (oncall-eng): @Zoe can you confirm Lysander impact? are they seeing billing alerts or just us?
Zoe (cs-lysander): They reported a sudden 4x increase this morning, emailed finance. They say it coincides with a heavy ingest job but their app logs dont show that many requests. asking for an immediate explanation.
Maya (oncall-eng): copying @Elena (billing) and @Samir for runtime/metric correlation.
Samir (eng-sre): I can take lead. first step: correlate runtime token emission with our metering service. pulling metrics.
Samir (eng-sre): quick queries:
```
-- runtime token count by tenant
select tenant_id, sum(tokens_generated) from runtime.events where tenant_id='lys-987' and ts > now() - interval '24h' group by tenant_id;
-- billing meter counts
select tenant_id, sum(metered_tokens) from metering.events where tenant_id='lys-987' and ts > now() - interval '24h' group by tenant_id;
```
Samir (eng-sre): runtime sum = 18.2M tokens. meter shows 72.5M tokens. wtf. filing hypothesis: duplicate ingestion path or double-count in metering pipeline.
Elena (billing): I can see meter shard logs show many duplicate ingestion attempts around 03:12-03:18 UTC from gateway-3. There are repeated ack replays. attaching small excerpt below.
```
[03:12:05] meter-ingest-3 INFO received batch tenant=lys-987 id=abcd123
[03:12:05] meter-ingest-3 WARN ack_timeout id=abcd123, requeue
[03:12:06] meter-ingest-3 INFO received batch tenant=lys-987 id=abcd123
[03:12:06] meter-ingest-3 INFO processed batch id=abcd123 tokens=120000
```
Elena (billing): those ack_timeouts seem to be causing duplicate processing - each requeue ends up counted.
Maya (oncall-eng): is this localized to dedicated pool or global? can we isolate?
Samir (eng-sre): looks like meter-ingest replicas in us-west-2 had degraded network to kafka leading to transient ack failures causing upstream retries. the runtime itself did not retry requests. so source duplication in metering pipeline.
Chris (ops-lead): mitigation plan: 1) pause metering consumer for lys-987 to stop further overcounting, 2) deploy dedupe filter in ingest path for requeued IDs, 3) compute customer-facing adjustment and issue temporary credit.
Maya (oncall-eng): stepping through handoff: @Samir you lead the technical fix. @Elena handle accounting adjustment and communication. @Zoe pls coordinate with Lysander contacts. I'm staying as incident coordinator.
Samir (eng-sre): applying immediate mitigation: creating a allowlist pause for tenant lys-987 on meter-ingest-3 to stop counting new duplicate batches.
Samir (eng-sre): ran command: `./meterctl pause --tenant lys-987 --consumer ingest-3` -> returns OK.
accounting-bot: Billing hold placed for tenant lys-987 (reason: active metering anomaly).
Samir (eng-sre): next, implementing an idempotency store for batch IDs. quick patch will keep a small in-memory LRU of recent message IDs to ignore replays. deploying to meter-ingest group with canary.
Samir (eng-sre): canary deploy in us-west-2-meter-ingest v2.1.1 -> 20% traffic. monitoring.
Maya (oncall-eng): monitoring dashboards: token rate for lys-987 dropped to expected after pause. good sign.
Elena (billing): preliminary adjustment calc: overcount ~54.3M tokens in last 12 hours. proposing 100% credit for suspect window and manual reconciliation after full audit.
Zoe (cs-lysander): Lysander asked for a timeline for root cause and credit. I told them we'll provide an interim credit this afternoon and a full detailed postmortem within 48 hours. they appreciate quick action.
Samir (eng-sre): postmortem notes for later: race between kafka ack timeout handling and internal retry logic. likely culprit: backoff config set too low, requeue immediately, causing duplicate ingestion if ack actually succeeded but ack message lost. needs durable idempotency at ingest boundary.
Chris (ops-lead): SLO/investigation tasks: (#1) full audit script to reconcile runtime vs meter by batch_id, (#2) durable idempotency layer story for Q2, (#3) update backoff/ack timeout to reduce replays.
Maya (oncall-eng): assigning tasks: @Samir #1 + #3, @Chris #2, @Elena handle credit + notify finance, @Zoe continue CS comms. I'll keep incident open until reconciliation complete.
Samir (eng-sre): putting a watch: I'll post reconciliation query results as soon as finished. leaving canary running.
incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 status updated -> mitigation in place. Severity remains P2.
Elena (billing): posted temporary credit of $12,400 to Lysander account for the suspect window and flagged invoice for manual review.
Samir (eng-sre): reconciliation run complete: matched ~98% of duplicated meter events to requeued batch IDs. attaching snippet of reconciliation output: 
```
replay_id, runtime_tokens, meter_tokens, matched
abcd123, 120000, 480000, true
efgh456, 64000, 256000, true
... summary: 54,345,600 extra tokens attributable to ingest-replays
```
Maya (oncall-eng): excellent. final next steps: root cause ticket to eng-runtime platform for durable idempotency, ops to schedule a post-deploy verification, accounting to finalize customer invoice and confirm credit, CS to confirm Lysander closure. I'll draft incident summary.
Zoe (cs-lysander): Lysander confirmed receipt of credit and is satisfied with mitigation. asked for postmortem.
Maya (oncall-eng): closing update: incident contained, duplicates stopped, credit applied, follow-ups created. moving to monitoring state.
incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 moved to monitoring.
Chris (ops-lead): thumbs up. will add action items to sprint. :white_check_mark:
